Resolve the title block of an output

Source: R/toc.R
tlf_resolve_titles.Rd

Looks up the titles and footnotes of program in a table of contents and returns a tlf_titles() object. There are three modes:

Usage

tlf_resolve_titles(
  program,
  type = c("Table", "Figure", "Listing"),
  sources = list(),
  scope = list(),
  number = NULL,
  pre_title = character(),
  source = "",
  vars = list(),
  on_resolve = NULL
)

Arguments

program

Program name, for example "t_demo".

type

Output type used for the banner when the TOC row has none.

sources

A list of toc_source objects, in priority order.

scope

Named list of scope values, for example list(study = "STUDY01").

number

Optional output number to pick one of several outputs produced by the same program.

pre_title, source

Passed to tlf_titles(). They come from the environment, not the TOC (for example a data cut-off line and the program path).

vars

Named list of placeholder values (see tlf_titles()).

on_resolve

Optional function function(titles) called after resolution, for example to write an audit record. Errors in it become warnings.

Value

A tlf_titles() object. $provenance records mode ("live", "snapshot" or "fallback"), the source label, the snapshot's generated_at when known, resolved_at, and why a fallback happened.

Details

  1. Live/snapshot. sources are tried in order. The first one that reads successfully and has rows is used, and later sources are not consulted, so a reachable live source is authoritative.

  2. Fallback. If no source can be read, or the program has no row, the result is a placeholder title block ("Table x.y.z" plus a "TODO: <program> title from TOC" line) and a warning is issued. The program still runs, so a dry run is never blocked by missing metadata, but a placeholder can never pass for a resolved title.

Matching: rows are matched on the program name (case-insensitive, ignoring a .R/.sas extension). A row whose scope cell is blank applies to every scope. Otherwise it must equal the requested scope value, and the most specific match wins. For scope columns not given in scope, general (blank) rows are preferred over specific ones. If several rows still tie, number selects one; a remaining tie is an error.

Examples

t <- tlf_resolve_titles("t_demo", sources = list(toc_source_data(ex_toc)),
                        scope = list(study = "STUDY01"))
t
#> <tlf_titles> mode: snapshot
#>   banner:   Table 14.1.1
#>   title:    Summary of Demographic and Baseline Characteristics
#>   subtitle: Safety Population
#>   footnote: Percentages are based on the number of subjects in each column.
#>   file:     t-14-01-01-demog.rtf
t$provenance$mode
#> [1] "snapshot"
